summary.value: The Slovenian Brown Hen is a laying breed created in the 1970s by animal scientists at the University of Ljubljana, working from Rhode Island Red stock that had long been a favorite on Slovenian farms. The birds are a solid dark brown with no pattern. Roosters have a metallic gloss and a tail of dark green and black feathers, and strong sun can fade the plumage. It has a medium single comb, orange eyes and yellow legs. Roosters weigh about 5.5 to 6.6 pounds and hens about 4 to 4.9 pounds, making it the lightest of the Slovenian layer breeds. Hens start laying at about 19 to 20 weeks and give roughly 295 to 305 brown eggs a year, averaging about 61 grams each, while eating less feed per egg than their cousins. The breed is also a parent of the Prelux commercial layers, and in 2020 Slovenia counted about 2,900 birds.
